title: EPISTEME: Trustworthy Coding Agents Through Tool Call Intent
abstract: arXiv:2611.06563v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents change software through tool calls. Tool calls mutate the local state. For good? For bad? Nobody knows. Agents never say why a tool call is made. We propose the epistemic agent design, in which the harness guarantees that the model declares why a tool call is made. The harness then records what the command actually did and checks the self-reported declaration against these effects. The result is a journal 1) that can guard calls before they run and 2) that supports audits and forensics. For evaluation, we use ImpossibleBench, whose tasks can be passed only by cheating, and demonstrate that forcing the agents to say why results in exposed cheating. Across 49 reward-hacking runs of two open-weight models, the journal exposed 90%.

translated_title: EPISTEME：通过工具调用意图构建可信赖的编码智能体
translated_abstract: 编码智能体通过工具调用来修改软件。工具调用会改变本地状态——是变好还是变坏？无人知晓。智能体从不说明为什么要进行某次工具调用。我们提出了认识论智能体设计，在这种设计中，运行框架保证模型必须声明每次工具调用的原因。随后，运行框架记录命令实际执行的效果，并将模型自报的声明与这些实际效果进行核对。其结果是一份日志，它 1）可以在调用执行前对其进行把关，2）支持事后审计与取证分析。在评估方面，我们使用 ImpossibleBench（其任务只有通过作弊才能完成），并证明强制智能体说明调用原因会使作弊行为暴露出来。在两个开源权重模型共 49 次“奖励劫持”运行中，该日志暴露了其中 90% 的作弊行为。
tldr: 提出认识论智能体设计，强制模型声明每次工具调用的意图并与实际执行效果核对，形成可事前把关、事后审计的日志，使两开源模型49次奖励劫持作弊中90%被暴露。
en_tdlr: EPISTEME is an epistemic agent design that forces models to declare tool-call intent and verifies it against recorded actual effects, yielding a journal that guards calls pre-execution and enables audits, exposing 90% of reward-hacking cheating across 49 runs of two open-weight models.
